units.en: The ⟦0⟧ allows the victors of a war to decide the post-war status of the losing ⟦1⟧ via a system of ⟦2⟧.
peace conference
countries
demands
Overview

During a war, belligerents on both sides accumulate war participation, a percentage that represents the relative contribution they make to their side of the war. The capitulation or conditional surrender of one side ends the war, computes the ⟦0⟧ of each victor based on their war participation, and opens the peace conference interface.
war score

The conference takes place over a series of ⟦0⟧. War score is distributed at the beginning of the conference if there is just one victor, or over the first five turns if there are multiple victors. During each turn, all victors may simultaneously select and submit demands for ⟦1⟧ or ⟦2⟧. If multiple victors submit conflicting demands, a ⟦3⟧ results and the victors may continue contesting it on subsequent turns until all but one have forfeited.
turns
states
ships
contest
Each demand involves the following roles:
⟦0⟧ – The victor making the demand.
Negotiator

⟦0⟧ – The country that will end up as the new owner of the demand. This is often the same as the negotiator, unless the demand is on behalf of another victor or is a demand type that results in a ⟦1⟧, liberated country, or forced change of government.
Beneficiary
puppet
⟦0⟧ – The country that loses the demanded state.
Loser

The cost of each demand is influenced by a variety of factors, including the type of demand, the value of the demanded state, the negotiator’s ⟦0⟧, whether the beneficiary has a ⟦1⟧ or claim on the demand, proximity of the demand to states owned by the negotiator, and whether another victor is already making a demand or contest on it. War score is a finite resource, so the player will often be forced to prioritize those demands that are most valuable to them.
ideology
core
The conference ends when all victors exit the conference, typically after all war score has been expended.
Interface
The peace conference interface consists of the following sections.
Score and turn panel

The top part of the peace conference interface displays world tension effects resulting from selected demands and the player’s currently available war score. Below the current war score is the current conference turn. To the right of this value is the war score that will be issued to the player at the start of the next turn and how many turns remain to issue the remaining war score.
Hovering over the war score values provides a tooltip summarizing the total war score the player is entitled to, including what is currently available and what they will receive in future turns.
Make Demands panel
The Make Demands panel provides controls to select the following demand types:

Take State demands – Annexes the selected state to the negotiator’s country. The player also has the option to select a different victor as beneficiary of the annexation by selecting its country tile in the Current Demands panel.

Liberate demands – Liberates the selected state to the country that has a core or claim on it based on game scripting. If the receiving country does not exist, it will be created. Its ideology will be the ideology of its original ⟦0⟧, unless it changes during the game, in which case it will be its last ideology before becoming ⟦1⟧.
tag
occupied

Puppet demands – Creates a puppet with the selected state or adds it to an existing puppet subject to the negotiator, if applicable. Democratic negotiators can only create ⟦0⟧ puppets from these demands.
supervised state
Change Government demands – Creates an independent country from the selected state, but its government will have the same ideology as the negotiator’s.
With the DLC ⟦0⟧ enabled, additional options include:
By Blood Alone

Take Navy demands – Acquires the defeated country’s ⟦0⟧ (carriers, battleships, heavy cruisers). Individual screening ships (light cruisers, destroyers, submarines) are not listed; instead, a proportional number of the loser’s screening ships are automatically included with the demand for each capital ship.
capital ships
Add Demilitarized Zone demands – Prohibits positioning military forces in the selected state for five years.

Add Resource Rights demands – Makes the state’s ⟦0⟧ available to the negotiator for five years. The resources depicted for each state on the map reflect the potential resources after upgrades and may appear higher than what will initially be received upon conclusion of the conference.
resources
Add Reparation demands – Provides half of the state’s current ⟦0⟧ to the negotiator for five years.
civilian factories
Add Dismantle Military Industry demands – Removes the state’s ⟦0⟧, degrading the defeated country’s ability to manufacture weapons.
military factories
The DMZ, Resource Rights, Reparation, and Dismantle Military Industry options are available only in conjunction with puppet or change government demands.

Selecting a demand type lists the demands available for the selected type, grouping them under ⟦0⟧. Country tiles represent either the defeated countries when take state or take navy types are selected, or subject/breakaway countries that will result when puppet, liberate, or change government types are selected. Green flag and red flag icons on each country tile provide an at-a-glance number of uncontested and contested demands for the associated country.
country tiles

Selecting a tile expands the list of demands available under the country. Hovering over each demand displays a tooltip with more details of the demand, including its costs, beneficiary country, puppet type that will be created, other countries contesting, world tension effects, etc. Holding the ⟦0⟧ key during this hover will display expanded details on the cost modifiers of the demand. Once bidding starts, small country flags on each demand indicate which countries are bidding on it.
Shift

Selecting a demand will add it as an ⟦0⟧ in the Current Demands panel and will deduct the associated demand costs from the available war score. Clicking the demand again will cancel the un-submitted demand, refunding the war score.
un-submitted demand
Current Demands panel
Selections in the Make Demands panel are added in the Current Demands panel on the right side of the interface, which consists of the Victors list and Beneficiaries list.

The Victors list is displayed by default and lists selected demands, grouping them under country tiles. Each country tile displays the country’s name, available war score, number of uncontested and contested demands, and war participation percentage. Selecting a country tile makes it the beneficiary of take state demands. By default, the player’s country tile is selected until another tile is selected. The current beneficiary is indicated with horizontal yellow bars.

Selecting the yellow arrow on the right side of each tile expands the list of current demands made by or for that country. Within the list, un-submitted demands are bracketed with yellow chevrons prior to the end of turn submission. Clicking an un-submitted demand will cancel it and refund any points that were deducted from the player’s war score. After the turn, if the demands go uncontested, the chevrons are removed, indicating that the demands are now submitted.

The remainder of each country’s demands list shows submitted demands from previous turns organized by loser and demand type. Victors cannot cancel their submitted demands from a previous turn unless another victor decides to contest it. When a victor leaves the conference, a green checkmark appears in its country tile.

Selecting the Beneficiaries button switches to the Beneficiaries list, displaying puppets and liberated countries that receive states from puppet and liberate demands made by the victors. This list is read-only and these countries cannot be directly selected in this panel as beneficiaries. Rather, their beneficiary status for a given state is determined by the available demands under their country tile in the Make Demands panel.
Interactive map

At the center of the interface, the map graphically represents the current status of different states during the conference, provides information based on selected demand types, and allows the player to select or deselect demands on states similar to the Make Demands and Current Demands panel. Hovering over a state displays a tooltip with demand information based on the currently selected demand type. This includes a breakdown of the costs. Holding the ⟦0⟧ key during this hover will display expanded details on the cost modifiers of the demand.

The map updates based on the currently selected demand type from the Make Demands panel. States that are eligible for the selected demand type and affordable to the player will be highlighted green. If the state is not affordable with the current war score, it loses its green highlighting. On selecting a demand, the associated state is highlighted blue. On subsequent turns, if the state has been successfully demanded without contest, it changes its base color to that of the new owner. If a state is contested, it is highlighted red.
Each state has an information card displayed on it with the following information:
War score points cost
Resources
Number of civilian factories (if Add War Reparation demand is selected)
Number of military factories (if Dismantle Military Industry demand is selected)
Flags of countries bidding on the state during the conference
A green flag to represent if the state has been demanded without contest
A red flag to represent if the state is being contested
Contested Demands window

If another victor submits the same demand as the player, on the next turn the war score spent on the demand is refunded and the Contested Demands window will display. The Contested Demands window displays the total number of contested demands, the total war score refunded, and a list of the contested demands.

The information displayed for each demand includes the new cost to contest it, the type of demand and name of the state or ship, and the countries involved in the contest. Hovering over a contested demand displays a tooltip with additional information, including details on other victors' demands. The player can individually select demands from the list to take action on or use the Select All button.

Selecting Close will close the Contested Demands window without making a decision. The Submit Demands button will be relabeled Contested Bids, and selecting it will prompt the player with the Contested Demands window to make a decision before ending the turn.
Selecting Forfeit will give up on the selected demands, allowing the player to keep the refunded war score. Selecting Demand will continue contesting the selected demands.
The decisions made in this window do not prevent the player from subsequently selecting or deselecting the same demands from the conference interface prior to ending the turn.
Other Controls

The Reset button, located at the bottom of the Make Demands panel, enables the player to cancel all unsubmitted demands within the current turn, thereby returning the war score to its original value. It should be noted that this button has no effect on any demands that have already been submitted in a previous turn.

The button labelled "Submit Demands", located at the bottom of the panel displaying the player's current demands, serves to submit all un-submitted demands and conclude the current turn. In the event that the player is unable to meet the financial obligations associated with the selected demands, this button will become inoperable. In the event that demands are contested, the Submit Demands button will change to the Contested Demands button. This will remain in effect until the player has determined an appropriate course of action within the Contested Demands window.

The Confirm and Exit button signifies the conclusion of the conference for the player and the closure of the peace conference interface. The button is only available when there are no longer any unsubmitted demands in the Current Demands list. Upon selecting the Confirm and Exit button, a warning is displayed, urging the player to ascertain that all requisite actions pertaining to the peace conference have been completed prior to exiting.
Conference mechanics in depth

The following information is provided to give players a much more in depth understanding of how the conference mechanics work and how various values are calculated. This information is subject to change in future patches, so the reader is encouraged to check the most recent patch change logs in case recent updates have outpaced the management of this article.
Participants
The conference initiates upon capitulation of the losing side, which may be:
A single country fighting the winner that is either not in a ⟦0⟧ or is in a faction but has none of its allies involved in the war.
faction

Multiple countries if they are in a faction and the ⟦0⟧ of that faction were all capitulated. Any non-major countries in the faction that were participating in the war will automatically be capitulated. Countries in a losing faction that were not involved in the war are omitted from the peace conference.
majors

Countries that are members of the winning faction, had been earlier occupied by the losing faction, and subsequently had half or more of their ⟦0⟧ occupied by a third-party faction fighting the losing faction (a common example is ⟦1⟧ at the end of the war in historic gameplay).
victory points
Poland

The winning side will consist of all countries, whether allied or not, that were at war with the losing country or faction. It is possible for victorious countries in a conference to be in separate wars against each other.

If a faction leader requests a conditional surrender via ⟦0⟧ and it is accepted, they along with their fellow faction members will comprise the losing side, and the winning side will consist of the faction leader that received the surrender along with their faction members. Other factions will be excluded.
diplomacy
War score
The peace conference begins with distribution of ⟦0⟧, a political currency used to bid on available demands. The war score awarded to each victor is calculated as follows:

⟦0⟧ = ⟦1⟧, where: s is the peace score scale factor, a constant in the Defines LUA file, currently defined as 1.35.[1] v is the combined state value of all states controlled by the enemy at the start of the war. p is the war participation of each victor, a percentage calculated by dividing the total of each participant’s war participation points into the total of all participants’ war participation points of the same side. c is a conditional surrender factor (only active if the loser conditionally surrenders) equal to the loser's surrender progress (represented by the red/blue bar at the top of the war summary window) at the time that they conditionally surrender.
